{
"Asynchronous Programming": "A programming paradigm that enables a program to perform tasks concurrently without blocking the main execution flow, allowing other operations to proceed while waiting for long-running operations to complete.",
"Async/Await Syntax": "A language construct, notably in Python, that provides a clean and readable way to define and invoke coroutines, using the `async` keyword to declare them and `await` to pause execution until an awaitable completes.",
"Coroutine": "A special function that can suspend and resume its execution, allowing cooperative multitasking by yielding control back to the event loop when awaiting an operation.",
"Event Loop": "The core runtime construct in asynchronous programming that schedules, manages, and dispatches the execution of coroutines, tasks, and futures within a single thread.",
"Task": "A unit of work wrapping a coroutine that is scheduled for execution on the event loop, allowing it to run concurrently with other tasks.",
"Future": "An object representing the eventual result of an asynchronous operation, acting as a placeholder for a value that may not yet be available but will be resolved later.",
"Callback": "A function registered to be invoked automatically when a specific event or task completion occurs, used to handle results or trigger follow-up actions.",
"asyncio.gather": "A Python asyncio function that concurrently runs multiple awaitables (coroutines, tasks, or futures) and aggregates their results, returning when all have completed.",
"Python": "A high-level, general-purpose programming language that provides native support for asynchronous programming through the asyncio library and async/await syntax.",
"Blocking Execution": "A mode of operation where a program halts and waits for an operation to complete before proceeding, preventing other code from running in the meantime.",
"Parallel Threads": "A concurrency model in which multiple threads execute code simultaneously on different CPU cores, distinct from the single-threaded cooperative concurrency used by event loops.",
"Polling": "A technique where the event loop repeatedly checks the readiness or status of tasks and I/O operations to determine when they can proceed.",
"Completion Handler": "A callback or function that is invoked once an asynchronous task or operation finishes, typically used to process its result or handle errors.",
"Execution Control": "The mechanism by which the flow of program execution is managed and transferred, such as when a coroutine yields control back to the event loop upon awaiting."
}
